newsitem.title: USA: WELLMAN SEES NO FINANCIAL EFFECT FROM FIRE.
newsitem.headline: WELLMAN SEES NO FINANCIAL EFFECT FROM FIRE.

text.p: Wellman Inc said Tuesday that a recent warehouse fire at its recycled fiber plant in Ireland is not expected to have a significant effect on operations or net earnings.
The fire occurred about two weeks ago, at the start of the traditional vacation shutdown at the Mullagh plant, the company said.

It began in a raw material warehouse and, ultimately, burned two out of five warehouses on the plant site. The contents of the two warehouses -- over two million pounds of raw materials and various supplies -- were destroyed.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation.
Wellman said it expects all of the damage to be covered by insurance.

The plant is expected to resume operations as scheduled next week. It will operate at a reduced production level in the near term until necessary equipment parts lost in the fire are replaced, it said.
Sales volumes are expected to be modestly lower as customers will be supplied with products from inventory and the company's recycled fiber plant in Johnsonville, S.C.
Wellman manufactures and markets polyester products.
